title: High-Impact Teaching Math Tools Without the Price Tag
shortDescription: Free math tools. Purposeful teaching. Make student thinking visible without another subscription.
fullDescription: Math instruction shouldn’t require another subscription. Experience free digital math tools paired with research-informed instructional strategies that make student thinking visible. Through presenter-led demonstrations and quick audience challenges, explore Digital Math Tools for number concepts, GraphSplat for data analysis and mathematical reasoning, and Quiz and Flashcard Studio for retrieval practice. See how modeling, argumentation, feedback, and problem-solving work together. Leave with TEKS-connected lessons, reusable activities, and practical ideas you can use without purchasing another tool.
learningObjectives: Identify free browser-based tools that support mathematics instruction.
Experience research-informed instructional strategies and discuss their purpose.
Use manipulatives, graphs, and recall checks to make mathematical thinking visible.
Plan a short classroom activity with a goal, strategy, tool, and evidence of learning.
Locate and adapt TEKS-connected lesson resources.
imageAlt: Illustrative classroom table with a graph, number line, and hands working with math manipulatives
successCriteria: Explain how a bar-chart baseline changes a visual comparison using values and units.
Choose a representation that fits a mathematical question and explain the match.
Outline a short lesson with a learning goal, strategy, tool, and observable evidence of understanding.

title: Project Management and Change Leadership
shortDescription: Turn a stalled initiative into a clear plan with shared ownership, useful updates, and evidence that the change is working.
fullDescription: A technical installation is only part of a successful school project. In this focused conference adaptation of the supplied project-management module, use one fictional district case to define scope, identify stakeholders and dependencies, plan communication, and distinguish delivery from sustained use. Experience brief models, individual thinking, neighbor discussions, and a small planning task you can adapt to a real initiative.
format: Presenter-led models with structured partner discussion
learningObjectives: Define a project’s purpose, scope, owner, and acceptance evidence.
Identify stakeholders, dependencies, risks, and the next decision needed.
Plan an update and measures that show adoption as well as delivery.
Draft and revise a small next-step plan after a neighbor’s feedback.
successCriteria: State an in-scope outcome and an explicit exclusion for the case.
Identify a dependency, an accountable owner, and an escalation trigger.
Propose a usable update and one delivery measure plus one adoption measure.
Revise a next-step plan using evidence and a colleague’s question.
